chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurarah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about reciting a chapter from the Book with which one supplicates in the prayer, such as 'Say: He is Allah, the One', so he said: 'If you supplicate with it, there is no harm.'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say: He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use Quranic chapters as supplications during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the practice of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas as a supplication (du'a) within the obligatory prayer, reflecting the Shia view that Quranic recitation serves both as worship and intercession. This ruling underscores the flexibility in ritual prayer regarding the selection of Quranic chapters for personal devotion, a practice widely accepted across Shia jurisprudence.
